lines.text: Ask your clients what language models do for them. You'll hear chatbots, copilots and agents. Now ask where their money is made or lost. Sales every minute. Payments every second. Readings from every machine. IBM Granite Time Series models are built for exactly that data. They forecast what's next, catch what doesn't fit, and turn both into a decision. That's the bigger prize, and it's in every account you cover.

lines.text: Here's one model reading six businesses at once: stores, payments, plants, deliveries, a checkout service and a building's energy. It was never trained on any of them. It forecasts each one from its own recent history, in milliseconds, on standard servers. Then a heat wave bends three forecasts at once. Every event is checked as it arrives: an empty shelf, card testing, a missed delivery, a slow checkout.

lines.text: For your client, three things change. Data teams replace hundreds of custom models with one. Planners get forecasts on day one, and they update with every event. And operations act in seconds, instead of the next morning.
